title: True unlimited esims
body:
O.P.
So, it seems TravelKon have stopped selling their Unlimited Max or True Unlimited esim range... the ones where data usage isn't shaped/throttled after X Gb is used.
Does anyone know of an esim seller who still sells unlimited esims that don't throttle usage?
I did some searching but couldn't find a vendor... not sure if that just means no one does them now or my Google Fu is out of practice.

---- replies ----
[User #168436•17396 postsHu_LionModerator] Mugsy writes...
So, it seems TravelKon have stopped selling their Unlimited Max or True Unlimited esim range... the ones where data usage isn't shaped/throttled after X Gb is used.
They still have that but it depends on countries and days you purchased for: https://www.travelkon.co m.au/product-category/esim/unlimited-esim/
For example this is unlimited for Thailand for 15 or 30 day: https://www.travelkon.co m.au/product/thailand-5g-esim-dtac
[User #6435613488 postsMugsyEnhance your calm!Whirlpool Forums Addict] O.P.
Hu_Lion writes...
They still have that but it depends on countries and days you purchased for:
I see.
The China one is now gone... but the current Asia 13 unlimited has 1.5Gb of high speed data daily and is then shaped to 1Mbps which is still decent i guess. It's not 128kbps which would be unusable.
Covers Singapore too so wife can use it on her stopover coming both ways.
Just need to wait till Black Friday sales to pick one up.
[User #6435613488 postsMugsyEnhance your calm!Whirlpool Forums Addict] O.P.
Hmmm, so I can either get wifey the unlimited Asia esim for ~$104 (usually) when it's on sale during Black Friday sales:
https://www.travelkon.com.au /product/asia-esim-unlimited-13-countries/
It'll be a single esim that will cover her entire trip from when she leave Brisbane till she returns.
Alternatively, I could get her the 100Gb esim which won't be throttled and hope that 100Gb lasts her whole trip:
https://www.travelkon.com.au /product/asia-esim-13-countries/
But she's used 15Gb within 3-4 days before. On that trip, I ended up grabbing an unlimited esim and messaged her the QR code to install.
So based on that past usage, which was an extreme case as she and her parents were staying at a hostel due to her mum going to hospital in another city and she was hotspotting for them to use internet too, a worse case scenario is that she'd need 150Gb to get her through the whole trip. I'd need to pick up a second esim for the last third of her stay in China... then probably grab one of those $6 Singtel esims from Pelago for her stopover in Singapore.
She'd need to dick around with installing and maybe configuring esims.
Maybe I should just stick to the unlimited TravelKon esim. Less hassle. I can install and check configuration here before she leaves. And she just turns on the esim when there (and turn off her Boost sim).
If anyone knows of an unlimited esim that:
has at least a 40 day duration
covers both China and Singapore
has a higher daily usage of 1.5Gb before being throttled
is throttled to no less than 1Mbps
I'd very much like to know of it.
[User #1610139004 postsPhil TThe only constant is changeSection Moderator] Mugsy writes...
Does anyone know of an esim seller who still sells unlimited esims that don't throttle usage?
I've only tried them once in HK so can't vouch for how well they work outside of there, but I came across ByteSim on my last trip. Looking at their app, for China there is an "Unlimited Data (*5G Network)" option (vs plans that allow for xGB per day).
One thing to consider is in some cases it is actually issued by a local carrier or MVNO (this was the case for my HK eSIM). Probably not as likely for the China eSIM, but some of the other country specific ones might come up as a local carrier vs a roaming one. (This was the case for the HK eSIM I tried out, so side effect was my Telstra AU SIM connected using the backup calling feature on the phone).
Edit – looking at your requirement list based on what I can see in the ByteSim app, the only one that can't be answered is the 40 day validity one (maximum 30 days is all I can see).
[User #6435613488 postsMugsyEnhance your calm!Whirlpool Forums Addict] O.P.
Phil T writes...
ByteSim
Thanks for the suggestion mate.
Yeah, it looks like 30 days is the max (as it is with many esim providers). The speed after one hits the daily quota is also 128kbps which isn't going to work... 1Mbps is lowest that'll be usable. Also not sure what the daily quota is.
Two other potential solutions I have found that only require a single esim installed but I can manage the purchase of datapacks remotely from my PC:
Roamless: I'd need to buy data packs for my wife and monitor her usage so I can buy the next data pack but she'd have full speed all the time (assuming I ensure there is data).
Eskimo: this one I've liked the look of for ages and should have looked at sooner... their standard data packs have a 2yr validity which means I can purchase a 10Gb Singapore datapack and anything left over can be used on her next trip (buying another datapack rolls over unused data from the current one). But they also have unlimited data plans too with a 3Gb daily quota before throttling down to 1Mbps! (I'm estimating 3Gb/day should be sufficient for my wife)
Max duration for unlimited plans are 30 days but unlike Roamless, I don't need to monitor by data left... I know the exact date her esim will run out before I need to buy another 10 days making it easier to manage.
Eskimo's dashboard shows daily data usage meaning I can finally collect reliable data on my wife's usage patterns in China
10Gb of Singapore data is AU$12.50
30 days unlimited is AU$80
10 days unlimited is AU$22.50
total cost is $115 which isn't that much more than the $104 for a TravelKon unlimited esim but only has 1.5Gb daily quota.
TravelKon can still get their hands on the true unlimited esims but only for China... they don't have one that'll cover Singapore too. Need to talk to wife to see if she wants to deal with juggling esims for true unlimited. I suspect she won't and will be happy to use Eskimo and let me manage the data plans purchasing.
[User #6435613488 postsMugsyEnhance your calm!Whirlpool Forums Addict] O.P.
Mugsy writes...
total cost is $115
Just realised that Eskimo's currently got a sale, but it's only 50% off first purchase up to $15 off.
Full price would be $171.50... kinda steep. But 2yrs validity for data and 3Gb/day unthrottled data may make it better than Roamless still based on my modelling of my wife's trip.
Another option... TheDoc suggested in another thread a Singtel esim bought through Pelago that has 700Gb in Singapore and 80Gb in 20 APAC countries incl China. Only AU$22.33. It's 30 Days validity from when registering with Singtel.
I'd have to monitor usage of this one but at 3Gb/day, it would last 26 days.
I can put the Eskimo esim on my wife's phone and test it in advance... there's a deal for 1Gb free global data that lasts 2yrs I can use for testing. Once I know it works, it can be turned off for use when my wife's Singtel esim runs out. It's $65 for 15 days unlimited with Eskimo and another $15 for 5Gb Singapore data. Would cost me $102 all up.
Alternatively, because redundancy is popular this week, I could purchase TravelKon's Asia 13 unlimited esim for $104. And the Singtel $22.33 esim... I know the TravelKon one works and is routed through HK so speeds are good. The Singtel one would be a test of routing through Singapore. Wife can use the TravelKon one first each day... if she gets throttled, she switches to the Singtel sim to maintain full speed. It's only a back up for about 28 days of course.
[User #6435613488 postsMugsyEnhance your calm!Whirlpool Forums Addict] O.P.
OK, I ended up doing some calculations.
1Mbps can download 400-450Mb/hr.
Streaming Youtube at 720p is ~1.5Gb/hr. For 1080p, it's 2.5-3Gb/hr.
There are some days the Mrs is streaming Youtube for possibly 3-4hrs when she and her mother are at the hospital and her mum is getting chemo. For perspective, due to the large population in China, nurses often teach family members how to change around things like saline solution or chemo drugs for the patient… there's not enough nurses to serve all patients like here in Australia. So yeah, wife and mother in law is there for a long time and need to pass the time.
Wife uses a Fold 5 so 1080p is the norm when playing on the big screen. That's probably 9-12Gb used on those days.
I reached out to TravelKon and they said they can get the old Max unlimited esim for China. It's 1Gb max speed then throttles down to 10Mbps... that's what the Mrs needs. No wonder last year's esim which throttled to 1Mbps was so noticeable to her. Esim costs ~$140 for 45 days... her parents are spending a few weeks in another city for her mum's cancer treatment so if the same thing happens when my wife does her trip back to China, she'll need this unlimited esim for sure. Also happy to support TravelKon so they can continue to provide these esims.
I'll just need to get another esim for Singapore... probably will go with Eskimo since it's the only provider I can find that will do a Singapore data pack for greater than 30 days (theirs remain valid for 2yrs), that I can manage remotely, and they have an unlimited option as a back up.
